text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert DD-9031 triggered — datadog ingestion delay detected for metrics/logs/traces (prod, us-east-1). Symptoms: high dd_ingest_backlog, webhooks failing with 429. Paging oncall.

alex: seeing large metric gaps in the latency dashboards around 13:04. spans/traces look fine but metrics/alerts are missing history. :eyes:

maria: confirmed — the agent logs on a few hosts show repeated `HTTP 429` to api.datadoghq.com and `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`. This lines up with Datadog incident(https://status.datadoghq.com) notice about ingestion delays. 

sre_lead: thanks. quick triage: 1) are customer-facing alerts firing (SLOs)? 2) can we switch critical dashboards to retained local/backup metrics? 3) notify product/support for potential customer impact.

sam: SLO alerts: a few internal alerting rules use Datadog metrics directly (e.g., inference-99p-latency-high). Those are firing as 'no data' which created noise. I've silenced those rules for the next 30m to reduce pager storm: `datadog silence add --tag prod --expire 1800` (ran at 13:12).

nyla: opening a support ticket with Datadog — I pasted our host agent logs and backoff headers. Also asked for ETA and whether this affects metrics ingestion only or also traces/logs.

alex: mitigation idea — flip critical metric collection to our CloudWatch mirror for the most important series (aggregate service.latency). We have a small Lambda that ships CloudWatch -> internal metrics store. I can enable that route temporarily.

maria: instructions to enable CloudWatch fallback (manual, because it's gated):
```
# promote cw-forwarder for prod
aws lambda invoke --function-name cw-forwarder-prod --payload '{"promote":true}' /tmp/out
# confirm forwarding to internal metrics pipeline
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PIPE_TOKEN" https://internal.metrics/api/check | jq .status
```
I can run this if oncall approves.

sre_lead: please do it, alex. We need last-mile visibility for customer-impacting dashboards and paging. Also reduce non-critical alerts. Keep me posted.

sam: FYI I rotated a few API keys for our Datadog exporters that were hitting strict rate limits. That reduced retries from some hosts. Not a full fix but less noise.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary release of cw-forwarder promoted to prod at 13:23 by alex (deploy id df-7783). Link: https://deploys.redwood.com/df-7783

alex: cw-forwarder promotion completed. internal metrics pipeline receiving aggregated latency for core models. Dashboards updated to show CW fallback series (prefix cw:service.latency).

maria: Datadog responded: ingestion delay is for custom metrics ingestion due to their internal queueing; traces/logs largely unaffected. No ETA yet, they said they're prioritizing critical customers. Asked for workaround doc.

sre_lead: good — we should prepare customer comms if Datadog ETA exceeds 1h. Product/Support: @maria please draft a short blurb for status page and support templates saying "partial observability degradation in metrics; we have fallbacks in place; execution unaffected".

maria: drafting now. Proposed: "We are experiencing degraded metric ingestion to Datadog which may cause gaps in dashboards and delayed alerts. We have enabled fallback metrics routing and silenced redundant alerts. We are monitoring; no customer RPC failures observed at this time. Updates to follow." 

nyla: also scheduling handoff to night oncall at 18:00. I'll collect timeline and action items into the incident tracker. 

alex: one more small mitigation — increased agent-side batching to reduce API call volume to Datadog while they recover. This should lower 429s.

sam: note: if Datadog resumes with backlog flush, we may get a spike of synthetic alerts once metrics flow again. Keep an eye and plan to unsilence alerts gradually.

sre_lead: agreed. Next steps: 1) monitor Datadog status and our internal queue (metric-lag) 2) keep CW fallback enabled until stable 3) prepare support/status comms 4) handoff to night oncall with runbook. Assigning nyla to do the handoff.

nyla: I'll do the 18:00 handoff. Adding runbook snippets to the incident doc: how to promote/demote cw-forwarder, how to silence/unsilence datadog alerts, and how to re-run agent key rotation.

maria: posting to status.redwood.com draft now. Also pinging a few enterprise customers directly (account teams) to let them know proactively.

incident-bot: Incident timeline updated in #incidents-log (inc-2023-1043). Link: https://incidents.redwood.com/inc-2023-1043

alex: monitoring — latency dashboards stable via cw fallback, but some derived metrics still show gaps. Will keep checking.

sre_lead: good work team. If Datadog provides ETA, we'll decide on longer-term mitigations (e.g., promoting cross-region mirrors or adding a dedicated ingestion contract). For now, keep updates in this thread and update the incident doc before handoff. :thumbsup:

sam: leaving a final note — retained logs for affected time window pushed to long-term store; we can retro-process if needed once Datadog recovers.

nyla: 17:58 manual handoff notes posted. handing off to night oncall (sam-night). Thread will be followed up if Datadog announces restoration or backlog spike.

sam: acknowledged handoff. I'll start 18:00 watch and update if anything changes.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident auto-acknowledged by oncall at 13:16. If escalated, use /pd escalate DD-9031.
